facts.statement: Conchoraptor was a small dinosaur measuring between 1 and 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Conchoraptor was a small dinosaur, only 1 – 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Unlike many other oviraptorids, Conchoraptor did not possess a head crest.
facts.quote: Unlike many other oviraptorids, Conchoraptor lacked a head crest.

facts.statement: Conchoraptor lacked teeth and instead had powerful beaks, which may have been adapted for crushing mollusk shells.
facts.quote: Instead of teeth, oviraptorids had powerful beaks, possibly adapted to crushing mollusk shells.

facts.statement: The skull of Conchoraptor was heavily pneumatized, meaning most of its bones were hollow.
facts.quote: The skull of Conchoraptor was heavily pneumatised, with most of the bones hollow.

facts.statement: Internal connections between Conchoraptor's ears functioned as resonance chambers that improved its hearing.
facts.quote: Internal connections between both ears functioned as resonance chambers and improved hearing.

facts.statement: The type species Conchoraptor gracilis was formally described and named by Barsbold in 1986.
facts.quote: The type species of this new genus, Conchoraptor gracilis, was described and named by Barsbold, in 1986.

facts.statement: The unique anatomy of Conchoraptor's hands was a primary factor in distinguishing it from Oviraptor as a separate genus.
facts.quote: The hands of Conchoraptor were a major reason scientists decided to split it off from Oviraptor.

facts.statement: The genus name Conchoraptor combines the Greek word for 'mussel' and the Latin word for 'plunderer'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek konkhè, "mussel", and Latin raptor, "plunderer".

facts.statement: Conchoraptor gracilis was discovered in 1971 by a Polish-Mongolian expedition in the Red Beds of Hermiin Tsav and described by Rinchen Barsbold in 1986.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Conchoraptor gracilis, fue descrita por Rinchen Barsbold en 1986, siendo descubierto por una expedición polaco-mongol en 1971 en la Camas Rojas de Hermiin Tsav de la Formación Nemegt.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Greek word for 'mussel' and the Latin word for 'plunderer'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego konkhè, "mejillón", y del latín raptor, "saqueador".

facts.statement: Fossils of Conchoraptor are known from the Barun Goyot and possibly the Nemegt formations in Mongolia.
facts.quote: It is known from the Barun Goyot and possibly the Nemegt formation of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The Baruungoyot Formation in Mongolia, where Conchoraptor fossils were found, dates to the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: The Baruungoyot Formation of Mongolia, is estimated to date back to the Maastrichtian stage.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the environment of the Baruun Goyot Formation was arid, featuring sand dune fields and only intermittent streams.
facts.quote: During the Late Cretaceous period, the land that is now the Baruun Goyot Formation had an arid environment with fields of sand dunes and only intermittent streams.

facts.statement: The Nemegt Formation in Mongolia is estimated to date from the Maastrichtian stage, between 70 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Se estima que la Formación Nemegt de Mongolia data de la etapa Maastrichtiense, hace entre 70 y 66 millones de años del período Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: During the Late Cretaceous, the Nemegt Formation featured an arid environment with sand dune fields and intermittent streams.
facts.quote: Durante el período Cretácico superior, la tierra que ahora es la Formación Nemegt tenía un ambiente árido con campos de dunas de arena y solo arroyos intermitentes.

facts.statement: Barsbold originally assigned Conchoraptor to the family Oviraptoridae in 1986.
facts.quote: Conchoraptor was by Barsbold assigned to the Oviraptoridae in 1986.

facts.statement: Recent analyses classify Conchoraptor as a member of the oviraptorid subfamily Heyuanninae (formerly Ingeniinae).
facts.quote: Recent analyses show it was a member of the oviraptorid subfamily Ingeniinae (now Heyuanninae).

facts.statement: Conchoraptor is classified within the family Oviraptoridae.
facts.quote: familia: Oviraptoridae

facts.statement: Conchoraptor belongs to the subfamily Ingeniinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Ingeniinae

facts.statement: A 2022 study suggests that Conchoraptor possessed a very strong bite force when compared to other oviraptorosaurs.
facts.quote: A 2022 study of the bite force of Conchoraptor and comparisons with other oviraptorosaurs such as Incisivosaurus, Citipati, and Khaan instead suggests that Conchoraptor had a very strong bite force.

facts.statement: The configuration of Conchoraptor's jaw suggests it fed on mollusks.
facts.quote: La configuración de su mandíbula sugiere que se alimentaba de moluscos.

facts.statement: Barsbold hypothesized that oviraptorids like Conchoraptor specialized in feeding on mollusks rather than primarily preying on eggs.
facts.quote: This name reflects Barsbold's hypothesis that oviraptorids, rather than preying primarily upon eggs as had been traditionally thought, may have been specialized to feed on mollusks.

facts.statement: It is debated whether oviraptorosaurs were powerful-biting generalists or specialists that utilized niche partitioning based on body size and cranial function.
facts.quote: The examinations suggest oviraptorosaurs may have been powerful-biting generalists or specialists that partook of niche partitioning both in body size and cranial function.
